spans.s:
Pṛdāku, the name of a ‘snake’ in the Atharvaveda,^1 is
mentioned in the list of victims at the Aśvamedha (‘horse
sacrifice’), in the Yajurveda Saṃhitās,^2 and occasionally else-
[]
where.^3 Its skin was specially valuable, according to the
Atharvaveda.^4
1) i. 27, 1; iii. 27, 3; vi. 38, 1;
vii. 56, 1; x. 4, 11 et seq.; xii. 3,
57.
2) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 10, 1;
Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 14, 14; Vāja-
saneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 33.
3) Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, vi. 12; Sāṅkh-
āyana Āraṇyaka, xii. 27.
4) i. 27. 1.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 94.

Pṛdāku-sānu, ‘having the surface of a snake,’ is taken by
Ludwig^1 and Griffith^2 as the name of the institutor of a
sacrifice in one hymn of the Rigveda.^3
1) Translation of the Rigveda, 3,
161.
2) Hymns of the Rigveda, 2, 141.
3) viii. 17, 15.
